title: Components
rule: Presenter controls drawn INSIDE the slide canvas are `<aha-button size="lg">` (40px), themed once with `applyCanvasDeck` from `lib/canvas.js`. Size only through the `size` attribute and colour only through `applyCanvasDeck`: never `::part(button)` overrides, never a raw `<button>`. This applies to build-less Developer Platform slide types; a built plugin that declares manifest actions has them painted by the host control bar instead. The other canvas components (count, status line, stepper) and any canvas panel or modal read the same call's `--aha-deck-*` ladder and container set, so one `applyCanvasDeck` inks the whole canvas for white and black ink.
why: The canvas is a cross-origin iframe that cannot see the host theme, so the deck accent, label contrast, hover and pressed fills are all set on the element by `applyCanvasDeck`. These demos are the shipped `<aha-button>`, `<aha-tooltip>` and `applyCanvasDeck`, not mock-ups. Moved here from the Button page; the Button page keeps every other size and variant.

sections.name: Presenter controls
sections.what: A row of lg buttons at the bottom of the slide: one primary, the rest secondary-deck, tertiary-deck only off photographic decks. A labelled button carries a `shortcut` chip; an icon-only button sits inside `<aha-tooltip size="lg" shortcut>` with an `aria-label` that names the key.
sections.useWhen: a control drawn inside the slide canvas (Reveal, Next, Start, Mute): size lg with the deck applied by applyCanvasDeck, one primary, the rest secondary-deck, tertiary-deck only off photographic decks; a shortcut chip on each labelled button, and an icon-only button inside <aha-tooltip size="lg" shortcut> with aria-label naming the key
sections.notFor: A built slide plugin that declares manifest actions (the host paints those in the presenter control bar), the app's own screens (use the Button sizes md and lg) and the audience phone (size touch).

rules.label: Canvas
rules.value: in-canvas presenter controls are size lg (40px, r8, 20px side padding, 16px / 600 label, 16px icon; icon-only 40 × 40). applyCanvasDeck (lib/canvas.js) sets the primary to the deck accent, its label black or white by contrast, hover 12% darker and pressed 22% darker, and the hover elevation to the rest one, so hover is a fill change only; secondary is secondary-deck, tertiary is tertiary-deck and never on a photographic deck (the action becomes a secondary). Scoped to the element it is applied to: app buttons keep every value above

The chip is display only: 24 × 24, radius 4, a 14px / 400 key that follows the presenter's machine (⌘ on a Mac, Ctrl elsewhere). An icon-only control keeps the key in its aria-label and shows it in <aha-tooltip size="lg" shortcut>. Hover is a fill change only.

sections.name: Correct / incorrect count
sections.what: The answer count many slide types show: a green check disc, the count and a person glyph, a divider, then a red cross disc, the count and a person glyph. Without `correct` / `wrong` it shows only how many answered, with no verdict mark.
sections.useWhen: a quiz-style result on the presenter canvas (`correct` and `wrong`), or any slide that shows how many answered next to its result (`answered`)
sections.notFor: the waiting state before a result (use the status line below) and the audience phone.

rules.label: Container
rules.value: the deck container set, small: 40px tall, radius 8 (`--aha-deck-container-radius-sm`), padding 8 on the disc side and 16 on the glyph side (`--aha-space-8` / `--aha-space-16`), count 16px / 600 with a 20px verdict disc and 12px check / cross, `--aha-deck-container-fill` and no stroke (a count is a small readout, so a line round it only adds weight). On a solid deck the fill is the ink at 8%; on a photo deck (`applyCanvasDeck({ image: true })`) it is the frosted opposite of the ink at 80%

rules.label: Colour
rules.value: only the two verdict discs carry colour (`--aha-answer-correct`, `--aha-answer-wrong`, white glyph); the count is the deck ink and the person glyph the ink at 76%. Never the accent

rules.label: Accessible name
rules.value: one sentence for the whole count ("12 correct, 3 incorrect"); pass a translated `label`

sections.name: Status line
sections.what: The waiting state as one component: the status line ("Waiting for answers…"). Free-floating deck text: no fill, stroke or scrim on any deck, photo decks included.
sections.useWhen: answers are still coming in on the presenter canvas and the slide shows what is happening
sections.notFor: a result count (use the count above) and any text that needs a backing to read: fix the deck, not the component.

rules.label: Text
rules.value: `text` replaces the line (`text=""` hides it); pass a translated sentence in the product

rules.label: Live region
rules.value: `role="status"`, polite; each change updates persistent nodes, so a new line is announced once

sections.name: Play
sections.what: The centred Play control on a video or media slide: a flat round disc on the primary colour with the play glyph, in md (48), lg (64, default) and hero (96) sizes.
sections.useWhen: one Play control sits in the middle of the presenter canvas before a video or media item runs (`size="hero"`)
sections.notFor: an action bar button (use the presenter controls above) and the audience phone.

rules.label: Disc
rules.value: a circle on `--aha-color-primary` with the white `system-play` glyph and no shadow: md 48, lg 64, hero 96 (glyph 24 on md, 32 on lg and hero); hover and press step to `--aha-color-primary-hover` / `-active`

rules.label: Focus
rules.value: keyboard focus draws the deck focus ring, a 2px gap in the deck background (`--aha-button-focus-gap`) then a 2px ring in the deck ink (`--aha-button-focus-ring`), both written by `applyCanvasDeck`

rules.label: Accessible name
rules.value: a native button named "Play"; pass a translated `label`. `disabled` makes it inert

sections.name: Stepper
sections.what: The shipped `<aha-stepper>` (Foundations → Stepper) registered as a canvas component, not a fork. On a canvas, applyCanvasDeck's ladder inks it: current stage in the deck ink with the 8% fill, done stages and the upcoming labels in the ink at 76%, upcoming rings in the 24% line, connectors in the 20% chip stroke, hover in the 12% fill.
sections.useWhen: a stage or round indicator on the presenter canvas (Ideas → Group → Vote → Discuss), size lg, paired with one primary Next button that keeps the accent
sections.notFor: the control that advances the flow (that is the primary button) and app wizards (use Steps).

rules.label: Ink
rules.value: `--aha-deck-ink`, `-ink-secondary`, `-line`, `-stroke-chip`, `-fill`, `-fill-hover`; with no deck applied it keeps its product colours, so slide types already using it keep working

sections.name: Leaderboard
sections.what: The ranked list of names and scores drawn inside the slide canvas: a rank chip, the name, the score at the end and a bar sized to the top score, all in the deck colours.
sections.useWhen: a slide shows who is ahead (quiz results, a game round, a team table): pass `entries`, set `size="stage"` and give the element a height; it fits as many rows as the height allows and ends with an "and N more" line
sections.notFor: a hand-built list of scores, a podium, or a ranking the participant sets (use rank-list)

rules.label: Row
rules.value: rank chip, name, score at the end; the bar behind the name is sized to score over top score (`bar="false"` turns it off); the name is drawn twice so the part over the bar reads on the fill

rules.label: Top three
rules.value: marked by shape, not hue: a trophy on first place and accent-filled chips on ranks 1 to 3; no gold, silver or bronze and no podium. Ties share a rank (1, 2, 2, 4)

rules.label: Deck
rules.value: themed only by `--aha-deck-*` tokens from applyCanvasDeck; teams (an entry with `members`) take the bar from `--aha-deck-palette-<n>`

rules.label: Motion
rules.value: rows slide to their new rank and scores count up with the DS motion tokens; none under prefers-reduced-motion
